instructor: Mr. Radushev is an experienced scholar and teacher with a rich past. He is very fluent in classes and never fails to attract my attention. He also incorporates small anecdotes from his life and past experiences which makes his classes much more interesting, enriched and informative. He skilfully and successfully ties the contemporary world to the distant historical world and makes you see the past as vibrant and alive. I advise him to anyone interested in not only the history of the Ottoman Balkans, which is his speciality but also to anyone who wants to learn and enrich their perspectives in history as well as contemporary politics.
course: The strongest aspect of the course for me had been the large component of geography which it involved. The course mostly adopts a Braudellian approach to history and emphasises the role of geography as overarching factors in long duration throughout centuries and even millenniums. It is of course a course on Ottoman Balkans, yet the incorporation of geographical facts allows one to think in broader perspectives over other time spans and see the continuities in the Balkan region throughout the past two millenniums, from the Roman times.
